text:
[LTIM.2.5.1] A rule gated on a time-dependent condition **must fire once per
false → true edge** of the condition for a given matched fact wrapper, on the
pump at which the edge occurs, and **must not re-fire** on subsequent pumps
while the condition remains true. This edge-once behaviour is a consequence of
refraction ([LDET.5.3]) with [LDET.5.8]: a clock tick is not a change to the
LHS, so a fired activation stays refracted across pumps for as long as its
match persists.

A pump that ends at a firing limit leaves the activation unfired; it fires on a
later pump if its match persists until then.

**A condition that closes ends the match, and a reopening is a new edge.** When
the condition goes true → false, the match ends and its activation with it, as a
`within` window's does ([LTIM.2.7.2]); no memory of the firing outlives the
activation. When the condition goes false → true again for the same wrapper, the
new match fires. A gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper; a
window that shuts and reopens, or a `now()` gate the wall clock crosses back and
forth ([LTIM.2.8.3]), fires once per opening.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_1__within_falls
idris.note: A `within` window on a fixed stamp changes at most once, true to false: it shuts and does not reopen for that entry, so 'a window that shuts and reopens' is a window on a new entry, a new wrapper.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__dwell_gate_rises
idris.note: WHICH GATES CAN REOPEN: a `dwell >= d` gate on a fixed stamp changes at most once, false to true, so it 'stays true once true' and the clause's once per edge is once per wrapper for it. Only a gate that reads the wall clock can reopen, which is [LTIM.2.8.3]'s last sentence.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__late_fires_once_clocked
idris.note: A gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper: `rule late` fires in the third of four pumps and never again, `[0, 0, 1, 0]`, on the composed engine.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_2__unfired_are_born_clocked
idris.note: What the pump after a tick fires is exactly the matches the tick made: one firing per edge, on this engine's timed chain.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__closing_ends_clocked
idris.note: 'A condition that closes ends the match': under the view, the re-timed chain holds no activation whose match the new test refuses, fired or not.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_once_clocked
idris.note: EDGE-ONCE ACROSS TWO SUCCESSIVE TICKS of this engine, for any gate: no match is made by both the tick to `c1` and the tick to `c2`, because the chain re-timed at `c1` carries the test at `c1` and the next tick re-times from it -- a match the second tick makes was refused at `c1`, which the first tick admitted. No hypothesis on the gate: Tick's `ltim_2_5_1__edge_once` needs `Ltim_2_5_1__rising` to carry a verdict from one tick's end to the next's start, and here the two are one clock. The clause's claim over a history -- a rising gate fires once per wrapper, the pump counts are the gate's rising edges -- is `ltim_2_5_1__rising_fires_at_most_once` (Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr) and `ltim_2_5_1__counts_are_edges` (Rete/NetworkEdges.idr).

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__expired_fact_cannot_reopen
idris.note: A wrapper that expired while the gate was shut is not there to reopen on: `[1, 0, 0, 0]`, computed. Once per edge is once per wrapper, and the wrapper is gone.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__reopening_is_unfired_clocked
idris.note: 'A reopening is a new edge': an activation whose match the tick made is unfired, whatever fired before the gate shut.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__second_edge_refires_clocked
idris.note: 'A window that shuts and reopens fires once per opening': `[1, 0, 1, 0]` over ticks 1 to 4 on the composed engine, computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_2367
idris.note: The window `{2, 3, 6, 7}`, the shape formal/tla/refraction_readings.tla and the conformance fixture `LTIM.2.5.1_window_reopens.json` share. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_2367_clocked
idris.note: ONE WINDOW, THREE MODELS: over ticks 1 to 7 the rule fires in the second pump and the sixth, `[0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0]`, one firing per opening -- the same answer formal/tla/refraction_readings.tla (`tick_edge_twice`, `1@2 1@6`), formal/tla/edge_once_firing.tla's `probe.refires` and the conformance fixture `LTIM.2.5.1_window_reopens.json` give.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_2367_gate
idris.note: That window as a time-dependent join test. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_2367_start
idris.note: The rule under that window loaded with one `Ping`. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_program
idris.note: The window rule's program. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_start
idris.note: The window rule loaded with one `Ping`. A fixture.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__action_free
idris.note: ACTION-FREE: every rule's action list is empty -- rules that only log, as [LDET.5.8]'s example does. The frame of B0 and B1.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__edges
idris.note: THE RISING EDGES of a gate over a history of ticks from a starting clock, one per tick: the clause's 'false to true edge', counted.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__action_free_mark
idris.note: Marking keeps a program action-free.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__action_free_tick
idris.note: So the tick keeps a program action-free.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__born_edge
idris.note: What a tick makes of one fact and the nil token: one match if the gate was false and is true, none otherwise. All four cases.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__counts_are_edges
idris.note: B2. THE COUNTS ARE THE EDGES: for one fact and one rule under ANY gate on the clock, with no actions and no deadline, the firings of ANY sequence of ticks from ANY starting clock are the gate's rising edges over that history, one count per pump. Once per false-to-true edge, for every gate and every history: a gate that stays true once true fires once, a window that shuts and reopens fires once per opening. Part A's `[1, 0, 1, 0]` is its instance.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_at
idris.note: ONE TICK'S EDGE: 1 where the gate is false at the clock before the tick and true at the clock after it, else 0.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_lt
idris.note: An edge count is below any fuel of two or more.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gate
idris.note: A gate on the clock alone, as a timed test: `now() > t`, a window, any predicate of the clock. A fixture family.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__held_at
idris.note: The one rule's activations when quiescent: the `Ping` match, fired, if the gate is true; nothing if it is false. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule
idris.note: ONE FACT, ONE RULE, ANY GATE: the clocked network holding one `Ping`, one alpha admitting it, one chain whose single positive node carries the gate at the clock, no actions, no dependency row, no deadline; quiescent at the clock. A fixture family.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_after
idris.note: What the tick and the run leave of the one rule's activations, from quiescence at the old gate value: quiescence at the new one. A gate that stays true keeps the fired match; one that closes ends it; one that opens makes a new match, which the run fires. All four cases.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_born
idris.note: The matches the tick makes of the one rule are its edge.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_pump
idris.note: ONE PUMP OF THE ONE RULE: from the quiescent state at a clock, the pump at a tick fires the edge and leaves the quiescent state at the new clock. B1 at the one rule.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_quiescent
idris.note: The one rule is quiescent at either value of the gate.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_tick
idris.note: The one rule after the tick and the run: the one rule at the new clock.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__pump_fires_the_born
idris.note: B1. THE PUMP FIRES THE BORN, on the composed engine: from a quiescent action-free state with an empty dependency table and nothing expiring at the new clock, the pump at a tick fires exactly as many times as the tick made matches over every timed chain, halts `Quiescent`, and leaves the state the tick made with every activation marked. Each born activation fires once and none twice. Inhabited by `ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_pump`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__run_marks_all
idris.note: B0. THE RUN IS ONE MARK PER UNFIRED ACTIVATION: under an action-free program, with fuel above the number of unfired activations, the run halts `Quiescent`, fires exactly that many times, and leaves every activation of every chain marked -- working memory, the alphas, the nodes, the tuples, the dependency table, the deadlines and the clock as they were. The frame is syntactic: a step under it is the marking of one activation and nothing else; a program with actions is outside it.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__second_edge_refires_is_an_instance
idris.note: PART A'S `[1, 0, 1, 0]` IS AN INSTANCE OF B2: Rete/NetworkClocked.idr's executed witness is the edge theorem at the window gate, from clock 0, over the ticks 1, 2, 3, 4.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_edges
idris.note: The window's rising edges over ticks to 1, 2, 3, 4 are `[1, 0, 1, 0]`, computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_start_is_one_rule
idris.note: The window of Rete/NetworkClocked.idr, loaded and holding its `Ping` at clock 0, is the one-rule state under the window gate. A TRANSCRIPTION: two definitions coincide, `Refl`; it fails if either is changed and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: iret_11_3__refraction_after_history
idris.note: The refraction the clause now rests on: after any history the `fired` flag on the activation is the whole of [IRET.11.3]'s set, and [IRET.11.3.2]'s clearings refuse nothing, so no pump boundary un-refracts a fired activation whose match persists. Tick-free here; that a tick is no change to the LHS and keeps the flag ([LDET.5.8]) is Rete/NetworkTick.idr's `ldet_5_8__tick_keeps_activation`, and the edge count through ticks is its `ltim_2_5_1__edge_once`.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__rising
idris.note: A gate that stays true once true: `now() > t`, the shape of every example in the clauses.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__late_fires_once
idris.note: THE CLAUSE'S OBSERVABLE, on the network: assert one Ping, pump twice with the gate shut, advance the clock past it, pump twice more -- `late` fires exactly once, in the third pump.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_2__unfired_are_born
idris.note: After a quiescent pump a tick leaves unfired only the matches it made: what the next run fires is exactly what the tick made true.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__closing_ends
idris.note: A CONDITION THAT CLOSES ENDS THE MATCH: after a tick, under the view, no activation is left whose match the new test refuses, fired or not. The match ends and its activation with it, as a `within` window's does; no memory of the firing outlives the activation.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_once
idris.note: EDGE-ONCE for a gate that stays true once true: two ticks, the second starting no earlier than the first ends, never both make the same match, so with `ltim_2_4_2__unfired_are_born` a match fires in at most one pump, on the tick its condition goes false to true. 'Must not re-fire on subsequent ticks while the condition remains true', on the engine with time-dependent tests and no tables. A gate that closes and reopens is a new edge, as the clause requires: `ltim_2_5_1__closing_ends`, `ltim_2_5_1__reopening_is_unfired`, and the executed `ltim_2_5_1__second_edge_refires`. On the engine with the tables, Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr's `ltim_2_5_1__rising_fires_at_most_once` is the count over any history.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__reopening_is_unfired
idris.note: A REOPENING IS A NEW EDGE: an activation of a match the tick made is unfired, whatever was fired before the gate shut. Under the view no old activation can carry that match, since the old test refused it; so it is one the tick made, and the tick makes its activations unfired.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__second_edge_refires
idris.note: THE SECOND EDGE FIRES AGAIN, as the clause requires: one `Ping`, one wrapper, never retracted; the window `(now() > 0 and now() < 2) or now() > 2` opens at 1, shuts at 2, reopens at 3. The rule fires in the first pump and in the third, `[1, 0, 1, 0]`: once per opening. Computed; what the clause says.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window
idris.note: `(now() > 0 and now() < 2) or now() > 2`: open at 1, shut at 2, open again from 3 -- the clause's window that shuts and reopens. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_gate
idris.note: The window as a time-dependent join test. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_loaded
idris.note: The rule under the window loaded at clock 0: one alpha for Ping, one positive node carrying the window, an RHS that only logs. A fixture.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_3__on_delay_fires_once
idris.note: 'Fire once per false to true edge ... and must not re-fire on subsequent ticks while the condition remains true': a `dwell` gate stays true once true, and the pump at 6 fires nothing. Executed.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_3__retracted_before_t_fires_nothing
idris.note: No edge for a wrapper that left working memory before the condition held. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__dwell_window
idris.note: A `dwell` WINDOW that shuts and reopens: `(dwell >= 2 and dwell < 4) or dwell >= 6`, logical/LTIM.2.5.1_window_reopens's gate. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__dwell_window_reopens
idris.note: A `dwell` WINDOW THAT SHUTS AND REOPENS FIRES ONCE PER OPENING: ticks 1 to 6 each followed by a pump; the window opens at 2, shuts at 4, reopens at 6 -- logical/LTIM.2.5.1_window_reopens's shape. 'A window that shuts and reopens fires once per opening.' Executed: `[[], [(0, True)], [], [], [], [(0, True)]]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__within_fires_once
idris.note: Once per opening for a `within` window, which opens at entry and shuts once. Executed.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__rising_b
idris.note: 'A gate that stays true once true', as a predicate of the clock.

idris.name: lexp_9_5_1__dwell_fires_once_executed
idris.note: 'A gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper', executed under `dwell >= 2`: `[0, 1, 0, 0]`, total 1.

idris.name: lexp_9_5_1__dwell_gate_rising
idris.note: WHICH GATES CAN REOPEN: `dwell >= d` is rising, so 'a gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper' is what it does; only a gate that reads the wall clock can reopen.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_at_true
idris.note: A tick from an open gate is no edge.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rising_edges_at_most_one
idris.note: C3a. A RISING GATE'S EDGES OVER ANY TICK HISTORY SUM TO AT MOST ONE: it rises once or not at all, because the composed engine's clock never goes back. 'A gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper', as a count.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rising_edges_none
idris.note: Once a rising gate has opened, no later tick is an edge.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rising_fires_at_most_once
idris.note: C3a ON THE ENGINE, with part B: the one-fact program under a rising gate fires AT MOST ONCE over any tick history from any starting clock. Once per false-to-true edge, and a rising gate has at most one. The hypothesis is inhabited by `lexp_9_5_1__dwell_gate_rising` and executed by `lexp_9_5_1__dwell_fires_once_executed`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__total
idris.note: The number of false-to-true edges over a history.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_gate_reopens
idris.note: 'A `now()` gate the wall clock crosses back and forth fires once per opening': `[1, 0, 1, 0]`, computed.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__late_fires_once_timed
idris.note: 'Fire once per false to true edge ... and must not re-fire on subsequent ticks while the condition remains true', for a `now()` gate. Executed.

idris.name: llog_3_11_1__clock_where_retracts_timed
idris.note: 'A condition that closes ends its match': the match ends at the pump at 3, with no change to its fact. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__alphas_two
idris.note: Two alphas, the Sensor's kind 0 and an unrelated Other's kind 1. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__expired_fact_cannot_reopen_timed
idris.note: AN EXPIRED FACT CANNOT REOPEN: the same window and advances with the Ping under a TTL of 2; open at 1 and fired; the tick to 2 sweeps the Ping, whose deadline is at the clock, before the pump; the window opens at 3 on nothing -- logical/LTIM.2.5.1_expired_fact_cannot_reopen's shape. 'Once per false-to-true edge of a live match', and the fact is not live. Executed: `[[(0, True)], [], [], []]`, and working memory empty.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__explicit_life
idris.note: An explicit lifecycle for every kind: the expired-fact fixture's Ping has no key. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__now_edge_once_multipump_timed
idris.note: EDGE-ONCE OVER FURTHER TICKS: after the gate opens at 6 and fires, the advances to 7 and 8 with the gate still true fire nothing -- logical/LTIM.2.5_now_edge_once_multipump's shape. 'Must not re-fire on subsequent ticks while the condition remains true.' Executed: `[[], [(0, True)], [], []]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__now_window
idris.note: THE WINDOW on the wall clock: `(now() > 0 and now() < 2) or now() > 2`, the witnesses' window of [LTIM.2.5.1] in their units. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ttl_two
idris.note: A default TTL of 2 on every kind. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__unrelated_change_timed
idris.note: AN UNRELATED CHANGE BETWEEN TICKS CLEARS NO REFRACTION: the gate opens at 6 and fires; a fact the rule never matches is asserted and pumped; the clock advances to 7 with the gate open; nothing fires again -- logical/LTIM.2.5.1.unrelated_change_between_ticks's shape, on the flag reading. Executed: `[[], [(0, True)], [], []]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_second_edge_refires_timed
idris.note: A WINDOW THAT SHUTS AND REOPENS FIRES ONCE PER OPENING: the Ping asserted at (0, 0); advances to 1, 2, 3 and 4, each followed by a pump; open at 1, shut at 2 (the match ends), open again at 3 (a new match), still open at 4 -- logical/LTIM.2.5.1_window_second_edge_refires's shape. Executed: `[[(0, True)], [], [(0, True)], []]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_2__now_edge_once_rearm_timed
idris.note: Once per edge of a live match: the first wrapper's one edge, then the second's. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__at_one
idris.note: A gate that can shut and reopen as the wall clock moves. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_gate_reopens_timed
idris.note: 'A condition that closes ends its match, and reopening it is a new edge': once per opening, under a wall that goes 1, 2, 1, 2. Executed.

tla.name: ltim_2_5_1__newpump
tla.note: A pump boundary. Under this clause edge-once is a consequence of refraction with [LDET.5.8], and a pump boundary clears no identity ([IRET.11.3]). The model keeps the event because the refused reading `pump`, which resets refraction each pump, is decided on it.

tla.name: ltim_2_5_1__pumpNo
tla.note: The pump number. Under this clause it scopes no refraction; it is the scope of the refused reading `pump`, and it stamps each firing in the observable.
